answer: Each applicant rents one numbered deposit box in a licensed vault and opens it in person with a passport, so one human holds one box. A 300 token bond sits in a sealed envelope in the box, and the vault logs each visit with time and photo. Over 90 days the agent signs 10 dated receipts, each countersigned by a clerk. Forging 1,000 identities means 1,000 boxes at 120 dollars each and 10,000 trips in person. Like an oasis holding water at its nadir, the vault keeps one real identity behind its door while fakes dry up, and a forger with a false receipt loses the bond and waits 180 days.
